analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: MIDTERMS (U.S. Equities Color, 3 Nov 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +37bps at 7,568 with a market-on-close imbalance of $2.3bn to sell. Nasdaq 100 +68bps at 28,180, Russell 2000 +40bps at 2,816, Dow -38bps at 51,786. Volume was 16.535bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.491bn.
Tech led a bounce ahead of midterm election results that night. Rate-sensitive areas underperformed as the 10-year yield rose 5bps to 4.96% after JOLTS came in at 7.523M vs the 7.164M estimate.
The GS floor rated overall activity a 4 on a 1-10 scale, with asset manager and hedge fund skews roughly flat.
Per Bartlett, the desk saw a more balanced two-way picture. Ongoing supply in semis/AI was met with select buy tickets, unlike the prior several sessions when supply met almost no defense.
Meta and Oracle both traded well after recent capital raises. The desk describes a 'paper-rich' environment concentrated in AI and calls the market's absorption of large issuance important.

Post-bell moves: ANET +6% on 3Q revenue growth accelerating to +59% y/y, the highest since IPO. AMD +7% on revenue and gross margins better than feared. PCOR +13% on a revenue beat and acceleration. BKNG -7% after-hours on guidance for a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights.

Derivatives: indices rose on geopolitical optimism ahead of the elections. Skew was sharply lower in gamma tenors in both SPX and NDX. NDX skew steepened in the belly and back-end while SPX flattened throughout.
SPX fixed-strike vols were little changed but were offered as spot faded into the close. NDX vol was bid, especially in gamma tenors, on spot outperformance.
Clients are swapping out medium-term vol expressions in favor of owning gamma in both index and single names, given the unpredictable, low-conviction tape.
Memory hedges were unwound and memory/semis upside was bought. A GS customer sold 10k WDC 15Jan27 300 puts.
The S&P implied move through the next day is 1.14%, vs 1.68% for the remainder of the week including that day. The midterm results are the main event, alongside earnings.
GS hosts a midterms event the next day at 10:15 am EST with its chief political economist, a policy analyst and desk heads from equities execution, EM trading and commodities.

market_movers.rationale: Stock rose 6% post-bell as 3Q revenue growth accelerated to +59% y/y, the highest since IPO.
Stock rose 7% post-bell on revenue and gross margins better than feared, especially after Intel's report last week.

Stock rose 13% post-bell. 3Q revenue of $402mn (+19% y/y) vs guide of $382-384mn (+13.3% y/y) and +16% y/y last quarter, including 2pts from the DroneDeploy acquisition. cRPO grew +29% y/y vs +22% last quarter.
Stock fell 7% after-hours on guidance for a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights.

earnings_insights: ANET reported 3Q 2026 revenue growth of +59% y/y (reported 11/3), the highest since IPO. Stock +6% post-bell.
AMD reported (11/3) revenue and gross margins that GS describes as better than feared. Stock +7% post-bell.

PCOR reported 3Q 2026 revenue of $402mn (+19% y/y, reported 11/3) vs company guidance of $382-384mn (+13.3% y/y) and vs +16% y/y last quarter. Includes 2pts of growth from the DroneDeploy acquisition. cRPO +29% y/y vs +22% last quarter. Stock +13% post-bell.
BKNG (reported 11/3) guided to a sharp y/y deceleration in 4Q room nights. Stock -7% after-hours.
